title: Keryx harness-config security audit report
description: planned — Output of `keryx security audit-harness` (W8, Design part A). No runtime emits this shape yet. Describes a point-in-time scan of every harness-configuration surface Keryx-aware harnesses read (instruction files, settings/permissions, MCP configs, hooks, W2 agent definitions, skill scripts, W4 imported bundles): per-surface coverage, per-finding severity/evidence/fix-proposal records, a deterministic 0-100 score with letter grade, and the baseline/suppression state applied to reach the reported totals. Findings never carry raw secret/PII values (leak-safe by construction, matching the convention already used by src/security/detect/mcp.ts).

schemaVersion.description: Report format version. Bumped only on a breaking shape change.

root.description: Project root the audit scanned, as an absolute path or a path relative to the invocation cwd (whichever `keryx security audit-harness` was given).

cliArgs.description: The flags this run was invoked with, recorded so a report is self-describing without needing the original command line.

surfaces.description: One entry per surface kind this run attempted to scan, whether or not it found anything to check — an absent surface (e.g. no .metaproject/agents/ directory) is a distinct, honestly-reported state from a scanned-and-clean one.

baseline.description: State of the suppression/baseline file applied to this run, or null when none was configured. A tampered baseline (checksum mismatch) is still reported here, not silently ignored — see `tamperState`.

severity.description: Shares the vocabulary already used across src/security/types.ts (SecuritySeverity) — no parallel severity scale for this report.

surfaceScanStatus.description: `not-applicable`: the surface has nothing to scan in this project (e.g. no MCP config file exists at all) and is NOT treated as a clean pass. `error`: the surface was discovered but could not be read/parsed; its findings list is empty and `coverage.status` for the whole report must not read `complete` while any surface is `error`.

pathsScanned.description: Paths (relative to `root`) this surface actually read. Empty for `not-applicable`.

pathsUnreadable.description: Paths that were discovered for this surface but could not be parsed/read; each contributes to `status: "error"`.

error.description: Human-readable reason when `status` is `error`. Leak-safe: names the path and the failure kind, never file content.

checkId.description: One of the check ids in workstreams/W8-harness-security-audit.md's check table (e.g. `mcp-tool-poisoning`, `unpinned-mcp-launcher`, `hook-command-injection`); additive over time, so not a closed enum here.

id.description: Stable identifier for this finding, deterministic given (surface, check, path, matched-signal) so the same underlying issue produces the same id across runs — required for baseline suppression to target it reliably.

confidence.description: Detector confidence, same 0-1 scale already used by DetectorMatch.confidence in src/security/types.ts.

path.description: Path (relative to `root`) the finding was found in.

pointer.description: JSON Pointer, for findings inside a parsed JSON config (e.g. an MCP manifest field).

message.description: Human-readable, leak-safe description of the finding. Never includes raw secret/PII/manifest content — matches the leak-safe convention documented in src/security/detect/mcp.ts (category token, not raw text).

policyId.description: Detector policy id when this finding came from an existing src/security/detect/* detector (e.g. mcp.poisoning.ignore-instructions).

matchedToken.description: A leak-safe token identifying what matched (e.g. "tool:search_web"), never the matched text itself.

fixProposal.description: Present only when a known remediation shape exists for this check. Never applied by the audit itself — see workstreams/W8-harness-security-audit.md Design A > Fix proposals.

suppressed.description: Whether this finding is currently suppressed by the baseline file. A suppressed finding is still listed (never dropped from `findings`), so the report is a complete record of what was found even when some of it is accepted risk.

id.description: Proposal id, used by `keryx security audit-harness apply --proposal <id>`. Never auto-applied.

rationale.description: Why this change resolves the finding.

patch.description: Unified-diff-shaped suggested change. Advisory text for the apply step, not a guarantee the apply step performs a literal patch application.

score.description: score = max(0, 100 - (critical*25 + high*10 + medium*4 + low*1)), computed over UNSUPPRESSED findings only. Deterministic and reproducible from `findings` + `baseline` alone.

grade.description: A: 90-100, B: 75-89, C: 60-74, D: 40-59, F: <40 — EXCEPT any unsuppressed `critical` finding caps the grade at `C` regardless of the numeric score (see workstreams/W8-harness-security-audit.md Design A > Severity model).

countsBySeverity.description: Counts of unsuppressed findings by severity, used to derive `score`.

totalFindings.description: Total findings including suppressed ones (== findings.length).

status.description: `incomplete` when any surface's status is `error`, or when a check that requires a prerequisite (e.g. `mcp-rug-pull` with no prior `scan-mcp --pin`) could not be evaluated. Mirrors the existing gdctx/security-scan convention that a required check which did not run is reported incomplete, never folded into a clean pass (see src/commands/security.ts scan-mcp coverage handling).

reasons.description: Leak-safe, human-readable reasons for `incomplete`, one per contributing surface/check.

tamperState.description: Checksum verification of the baseline file, using the same mechanism already used for .metaproject/security.config.json (src/security/config.ts verifyConfigChecksum). `mismatch` or `unreadable` is itself a --ci gate failure (see W8-AC8).

justification.description: Required, non-empty. A baseline entry with no justification fails schema validation — suppression is never silent.

expiresAt.description: Null/absent is valid but is itself flagged by the audit as a low-severity `indefinite-suppression` finding (see W8-AC7) — baseline rot is visible, not blocked.
